questions.question: Which ancient Wonder of the World is the only one that still largely stands intact today?
questions.explanation: Built circa 2560 BC for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest and only surviving Wonder of the Ancient World.
questions.funFact: The Great Pyramid was the tallest man-made structure on Earth for over 3,800 years!

questions.question: Which Roman Emperor famously made his beloved horse Incitatus a Roman senator (or promised to)?
questions.explanation: Emperor Caligula pampered his horse with an ivory stable, purple blankets, and threatened to appoint him consul to mock the Senate.
questions.funFact: Caligula's real name was Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus Germanicus; 'Caligula' means 'Little Boot'!

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in Agra after Mumtaz Mahal died in 1631; it was completed around 1653.
questions.funFact: Around 20,000 workers are said to have worked on it for about two decades.

questions.question: Which Mauryan emperor embraced Buddhism after the bloody Kalinga War?
questions.explanation: Ashoka was so moved by the suffering in the Kalinga War (about 261 BC) that he gave up conquest and spread Buddhism and non-violence.
questions.funFact: The lion capital from his pillar at Sarnath is India's national emblem.

questions.question: Who founded the Mauryan Empire with guidance from the scholar Chanakya?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda dynasty around 321 BC and built one of ancient India's largest empires.
questions.funFact: Chanakya is also credited with writing the Arthashastra, a text on statecraft.

questions.question: Which battle in 1526 established the Mughal Empire in India?
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi of the Delhi Sultanate at Panipat, using gunpowder and field artillery.
questions.funFact: Babur was a descendant of both Timur and Genghis Khan.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey in 1757 helped which power gain control over Bengal?
questions.explanation: Robert Clive's victory over Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah, helped by Mir Jafar's betrayal, laid the foundation for British rule in India.
questions.funFact: The battle lasted only about a day.

questions.question: Which ruler was known as the 'Tiger of Mysore' and died defending Srirangapatna in 1799?
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan fought the British in the Anglo-Mysore Wars and was killed in the siege of Srirangapatna in 1799.
questions.funFact: He used war rockets that later inspired British rocket technology.

questions.question: Who is credited with founding Bengaluru in 1537?
questions.explanation: Kempe Gowda I, a chieftain under the Vijayanagara Empire, built a mud fort and laid out the city in 1537.
questions.funFact: He placed four watchtowers marking how far he thought the city would grow.

questions.question: Can the Great Wall of China be seen from space with the naked eye?
options: No, this is a popular myth
questions.explanation: Astronauts say the wall is too narrow to be seen without aid from orbit, and it can't be seen from the Moon at all.
questions.funFact: The Wall is made up of many separate walls built over more than 2,000 years.

questions.question: Cleopatra lived closer in time to which event than to the building of the Great Pyramid?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC, over 2,500 years before Cleopatra, who died in 30 BC, about 2,000 years before the 1969 Moon landing.
questions.funFact: Cleopatra was actually from a Greek-Macedonian dynasty, the Ptolemies.

questions.question: Which discovery allowed scholars to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs?
questions.explanation: The Rosetta Stone carries the same decree in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek, and Jean-Francois Champollion cracked the code in 1822.
questions.funFact: It was found by French soldiers in 1799 and is now in the British Museum.

questions.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu in the Andes?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu was built around the mid-1400s under the Inca ruler Pachacuti and abandoned during the Spanish conquest.
questions.funFact: Hiram Bingham brought it to world attention in 1911.

questions.question: Who founded the Mongol Empire in 1206?
questions.explanation: Temujin was proclaimed Genghis Khan and united the Mongol tribes, starting the largest contiguous land empire in history.
questions.funFact: At its peak, the empire stretched from Korea to Eastern Europe.

questions.question: Alexander the Great died in 323 BC in which city?
questions.explanation: Alexander died in Babylon at about 32 years old, after never losing a major battle.
questions.funFact: The cause of his death is still debated.

questions.question: On which date was Julius Caesar assassinated in 44 BC?
questions.explanation: A group of senators including Brutus and Cassius stabbed Caesar on the Ides of March.
questions.funFact: He was reportedly stabbed 23 times.

questions.question: Roughly how many spectators could the Roman Colosseum hold?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum could host roughly 50,000 spectators for gladiator fights and public spectacles.
questions.funFact: It could reportedly be emptied in minutes thanks to its 80 entrances.

questions.question: Which Viking explorer is believed to have reached North America around the year 1000?
questions.explanation: Norse explorer Leif Erikson landed in a place he called Vinland, about 500 years before Columbus.
questions.funFact: Archaeologists confirmed a Norse site at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland.

questions.question: In which year did Christopher Columbus first reach the Americas?
questions.explanation: Columbus sailed under the Spanish crown and landed in the Bahamas in October 1492, while searching for a route to Asia.
questions.funFact: He died believing he had reached Asia.

questions.question: Roughly what share of Europe's population did the Black Death kill in the 1300s?
options: About a third to a half
questions.explanation: The plague from 1347 to 1351 killed an estimated 30 to 50% of Europe's people.
questions.funFact: It is thought to have spread via fleas on rats along trade routes.

questions.question: Which English king was forced to seal the Magna Carta in 1215?
questions.explanation: Rebel barons made King John agree to limits on royal power, an early step toward constitutional law.
questions.funFact: Only four of the original 1215 copies survive.

questions.question: Which Ottoman sultan conquered Constantinople in 1453?
questions.explanation: Mehmed II, aged 21, captured the city and ended the Byzantine Empire.
questions.funFact: The Ottomans used enormous cannons to break the ancient walls.

questions.question: The French Revolution is commonly said to have begun with the storming of which fortress in 1789?
questions.explanation: On 14 July 1789, Parisians stormed the Bastille prison, which became a symbol of the revolution.
questions.funFact: France still celebrates 14 July as Bastille Day.

questions.question: Where was Napoleon exiled after his defeat at Waterloo in 1815?
questions.explanation: The British sent Napoleon to remote Saint Helena in the South Atlantic, where he died in 1821.
questions.funFact: Earlier, he had escaped from exile on the island of Elba.

questions.question: In which year did the Titanic sink?
questions.explanation: The RMS Titanic hit an iceberg on 14 April 1912 and sank in the early hours of 15 April on her maiden voyage.
questions.funFact: Only about a third of the roughly 2,200 people on board survived.

questions.question: The assassination of which archduke in Sarajevo sparked World War I?
questions.explanation: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary was shot by Gavrilo Princip on 28 June 1914.
questions.funFact: The war began about a month later.

questions.question: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: East Germany opened the border on 9 November 1989, and Germany reunified in 1990.
questions.funFact: The wall had stood since 1961.

questions.question: Where is Stonehenge located?
questions.explanation: Stonehenge stands on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, with construction beginning around 3000 BC.
questions.funFact: Some of its bluestones were brought from Wales, about 240 km away.

questions.question: What is the native name of Easter Island, famous for its giant moai statues?
questions.explanation: Rapa Nui belongs to Chile and has nearly 1,000 moai carved by the Polynesian islanders.
questions.funFact: The statues are mostly heads and torsos, but many have buried bodies below.

questions.question: What is a big unsolved mystery of the Indus Valley Civilization?
options: Its script has never been deciphered
questions.explanation: Symbols found on seals at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro remain undeciphered despite decades of study.
questions.funFact: The cities had advanced drainage systems around 2500 BC.

questions.question: Nalanda, one of the world's oldest universities, was located in which modern Indian state?
questions.explanation: Nalanda flourished from around the 5th century AD and drew scholars from across Asia, before being destroyed in the 12th century.
questions.funFact: It reportedly had a library so huge that it burned for months.

questions.question: What word was found carved on a post after the 'Lost Colony' of Roanoke vanished?
questions.explanation: When John White returned in 1590, the settlers had disappeared, leaving only the word CROATOAN carved on a post.
questions.funFact: Their fate remains one of America's oldest mysteries.

questions.question: The ship Mary Celeste was found in 1872 in what state?
questions.explanation: The ship was found adrift in the Atlantic, seaworthy but with nobody on board, and the crew were never found.
questions.funFact: Its cargo of alcohol was mostly untouched.

questions.question: What is the Voynich Manuscript, held at Yale?
options: An undeciphered book in an unknown script
questions.explanation: The 15th-century book is filled with strange plants and diagrams in a script nobody has been able to read.
questions.funFact: Theories range from a hoax to a lost language.

questions.question: The Antikythera mechanism, found in a shipwreck, is thought to be what?
questions.explanation: This bronze gear device from about the 2nd century BC tracked the movements of the Sun, Moon and planets.
questions.funFact: Nothing as complex appeared again for over a thousand years.

questions.question: Who was buried with the Terracotta Army in China?
options: Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor
questions.explanation: The thousands of clay soldiers guard the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, who unified China in 221 BC.
questions.funFact: Local farmers found it in 1974 while digging a well.

questions.question: The great Library of Alexandria was located in which country?
questions.explanation: The library, founded in the Ptolemaic period, aimed to collect all the world's knowledge in Alexandria, Egypt.
questions.funFact: How and when it was destroyed is still debated by historians.

questions.question: Which volcano buried the Roman city of Pompeii in 79 AD?
questions.explanation: Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in ash and pumice, preserving them for centuries.
questions.funFact: Some victims were preserved in ash as detailed body casts.

questions.question: In which year did the Ottoman Sultanate formally end?
questions.explanation: The Ottoman Sultanate was abolished in 1922, and Turkey became a republic in 1923 under Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.
questions.funFact: The empire had lasted over 600 years.

questions.question: The Aztec capital Tenochtitlan lies beneath which modern city?
questions.explanation: Founded in 1325 on an island in Lake Texcoco, Tenochtitlan was conquered by Hernan Cortes in 1521.
questions.funFact: It had causeways, canals and floating gardens.

questions.question: Mansa Musa, one of the richest people in history, ruled which empire?
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca, with lots of gold, reportedly caused inflation in the places he visited.
questions.funFact: Timbuktu became a major centre of learning under his rule.

questions.question: Who was the first emperor to unify China in 221 BC?
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang unified the warring states, standardised writing and measures, and began the early Great Wall.
questions.funFact: The word 'China' is thought to derive from 'Qin'.

questions.question: Which queen led the 1857 revolt at Jhansi against the British?
questions.explanation: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi fought the British in the Indian Rebellion of 1857 and died in battle in 1858.
questions.funFact: She is said to have fought with her infant son tied to her back.

questions.question: Gandhi's Salt March in 1930 ended at which coastal village?
questions.explanation: Gandhi walked about 390 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to protest the British salt tax.
questions.funFact: The march took about 24 days.

questions.question: Which Chola king built the Brihadisvara Temple in Thanjavur?
questions.explanation: Raja Raja Chola I completed this UNESCO World Heritage temple around 1010 AD.
questions.funFact: Its main tower is about 66 m tall.

questions.question: Hampi in Karnataka was the capital of which empire?
questions.explanation: Hampi was the centre of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka.
questions.funFact: Foreign visitors once described it as one of the richest cities in the world.

questions.question: Whose expedition completed the first voyage around the world (1519-1522)?
questions.explanation: Magellan's fleet completed the circumnavigation after he died in the Philippines, under Juan Sebastian Elcano.
questions.funFact: Only 18 of about 240 men made it back.

questions.question: Which invention by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440 transformed Europe?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg's press in Mainz made books cheaper and helped spread ideas during the Renaissance and Reformation.
questions.funFact: His famous Bible was among the first major books printed in Europe.

questions.question: Which Greek hero is credited with devising the Trojan Horse plan?
questions.explanation: In Greek legend, Odysseus came up with hiding soldiers in a wooden horse to enter Troy.
questions.funFact: The story appears in later texts like Virgil's Aeneid, not in Homer's Iliad.

questions.question: The Silk Road was a network of trade routes linking China with which region?
questions.explanation: The Silk Road connected China with India, Persia and the Mediterranean, carrying silk, spices, paper and ideas.
questions.funFact: It was not one road but many routes, and ideas like Buddhism travelled along it too.
